subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should legacy ownerless session rows be permanently fail-closed to plugin-runtime `sessions.patch`, or should OpenClaw provide a migration or operator recovery path before enforcement?
rationale: This choice changes persisted authority and upgrade behavior for existing plugin workflows; the current delete fence supports fail-closed isolation but does not by itself establish the intended recovery contract for all legacy patch users.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Keep ownerless rows denied, document an operator recovery path, and require upgrade and runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Migrate ownership
options.body: Add a doctor or explicit owner-assignment migration before enforcing the new denial.

options.title: Defer legacy policy
options.body: Land only foreign-owned row rejection and track ownerless-row authority as separate work.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows denied, document an operator recovery path, and require upgrade and runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing session projection and plugin-runtime delete ownership behavior appear to originate in his current-main work.
